name: Paper / Vox explainer
look: A paper tabletop: prints, cut-outs with white keylines, typed strips, rubber stamps, newspapers, sticky notes, ledger arithmetic; things drop, slide and stamp in. Hard cuts, full sound design.

devices.use: Paper tabletop: photo prints (pc), cut-out props (cutout), typed strips, rubber stamps, sticky notes, circles and arrows - each lands on its word. The workhorse of the paper look: most explanations happen here.

Cut-out props inside collages (k='cut'): the kit has 47 in media/kit/cutouts (books, envelopes, labels, the newspaper globe...), or cut one from a photo with cutout(). Vox look references: media/kit/vox/*.jpg
Kinetic type: one to three big words slam in on the beat (items=[W_('...')]). The punch of a sentence, the question, the twist.
One big number that counts up, with a kicker and a note. Every important figure the narrator says.
Claims sorted into folders: known / claimed / unknown. The video's argument made visible.
Headlines slam in one after another - 'everyone reported it', a wave of coverage.
Full-screen chapter card: number, kicker, title. One per act.
A quotation set large with who said it and highlighted words. Every time the script quotes someone.
Depth pop: the subject is cut out of the photo and grows while the ground darkens and blurs. Use when the narration names a real person, place or object - never private people.
Everything but one circle darkens and blurs; a label points at the subject. 'Look here' moments: the detail that matters in a photo.
The animated map: the camera flies between places, pins drop, routes draw, regions light up. Every place the narration names gets one (group nearby places into one map scene).
Dates on a line; events appear in order. Any 'in 1990... by 2000... today' passage.
Points ticked off one by one: requirements, reasons, steps, 'three things...'.
A size comparison: the object against a known scale (people, buses, football fields).
A newspaper page with headline and photo; the camera moves into the article. 'It was reported that...'.
An account that adds up line by line to a total: costs, counts, a running sum.

The picture plays inside an old TV set and the camera pushes into the screen. 'Back then', archive, broadcast, 'on the news' moments. Mark archive shots archive=True to also get the vintage TV-gate overlay.
Two pictures side by side with labels: before / after, then / now, A vs B.
A document, scan, letter or clipping held as a card with a slow zoom: records, evidence, official papers.
A terrain / satellite close-up of a region with labels and a profile: mountains, valleys, where exactly.
The title card of the video.

also_available: every engine device works in every template; the list above is this template's vocabulary and its minimums
rules: Every sentence gets the picture that shows what it says, landing on its words ('@words' timing).
Never two plain shots of the same kind for long: break runs of clips/photos with the template's devices.
Every number the narrator stresses is SHOWN with a number device; every place named is SHOWN on a map; every quotation is set as a quote.
No clip or picture twice in the same video; no talking heads, influencers, watermarks or logos (QC enforces it).
Look at the preview of each device (docu/templates/previews/<theme>/<device>.jpg) and copy its gallery spec as the starting point.
Explain on paper: most explanations are collages built from prints, cut-out props and typed strips that land on their words.
Stamp the verdicts (CLAIMED, UNPROVEN...) and slam the punch words.
Hard cuts; sound on every drop, stamp and slam.
